transcript: Last night I saw Once Upon a One More Time on Broadway, a new jukebox musical that mixes fairy tale characters with Britney Spears music. In a world where fairy tale characters perpetually live and perform their stories for children as bedtime stories, Cinderella begins to wonder if there could be more to life than just marrying Prince Charming and living happily ever after. She and the other princesses begin to realize how limited their worldview has been trapped inside these outdated and oftentimes problematic fairy tales, and they seek more independence and autonomy over their own ever afters. The incorporation of the music is pretty good, although some of the lyric changes to make them fit more literally into the story I felt were a little bit clunky and unnecessary. I also thought the book and the music arrangements were a little bit uneven, especially in terms of suiting the pop music to the more musical theatre voices. But I thought the choreo was amazing and I was thoroughly entertained. The show really delivers on big ensemble numbers. With that, another playbill for my collection.

The overall tone is moderately positive but with enough caveats to place it in the mixed range.
